title: Signoff v2 reviewer answer
description: What the independent reviewer reports back, as the executor hands it to `record-answer`. This schema fixes the SHAPE only. The evidence rules - a location inside the source set, a claim, a scenario and an evidence kind on every finding - are deliberately NOT required here: a finding missing one of them must reach the adjudication so the run can refuse the answer as `answer_invalid` with the field named, rather than dying as a schema error that says nothing about which rule the reviewer broke. A recorded answer replayed from a file has exactly this shape, which is why a seeded case can stand in for a live reviewer.

seeded_answer.description: the seeded-case shape version, when the answer came from one

case.description: the seeded case this answer belongs to, when it came from one

session_id.description: the session that produced this answer. Equal to the input's building session is the independence refusal

model.description: the model the run OBSERVED, never one it assumed: readers' effective model as the adapter's sidecar map hands it over (`answer_identity.model`). The core takes the reviewer's floor from it (Astra's F5): missing, below the Opus-class floor, or not the session's recorded model refuses the answer (`refusal_reason: floor`)

checks_executed.description: every check the reviewer ran, with its output. A review with no findings and no entry here is not a clean verdict

findings.description: what the reviewer would raise. Each entry is checked against the evidence rules by the adjudication, not by this schema

notes_kept.description: what the reviewer kept as a note rather than raising: a plausible defect its own execution disproved, for instance

verdict.description: the verdict the reviewer states; the severity mapping is computed beside it
